item.title: Dublin Literary Award Longlist Announced
item.description: The Dublin Literary Award, an annual award which seeks to spotlight books from around the world through nominations from public libraries, has announced its longlist for 2026. The Award seeks to collaborate with libraries in Dublin and worldwide to support work both from Ireland and abroad, with a prize worth €100,000 for a single work of English or translated fiction. item.title: Luke and Máire to be Wed in the Big Fat Trinity Wedding
item.description: On the 13th of February, at Pav Friday, as part of the Big Fat Trinity Wedding, one of six couples was engaged and set to be married. The six couples competing to be wed were: Freddie and Geoffrey, Kiana and Josie, Molly and Seb, Auguste and Oscar, Teddy and Michael, and Luke and Maire. Each couple led their own pub crawl on the 11th of February in order for the attendees to decide who they would vote for via donations. item.title: Boycotting Spotify
item.description: Within the past decade, Spotify has secured itself a position as the default platform for music streaming to the extent that it has become synonymous with the music listening experience itself. Playlist culture has redefined how an entire generation of artists and listeners create and consume music, and advertising campaigns like Spotify Wrapped have become cultural events. item.title: Thirty Years of Glad: The Endless Relevance of Infinite Jest
item.description: In 1994, American essayist and literary critic Sven Birkerts predicted that the birth of the internet age would bring about the death of a certain reading experience: the virtuoso novels of Steinbeck or Pynchon that facilitate a prolonged, all-consuming immersion were withering away, and our attention was shifting to entertainment with a more instant gratification. item.title: In Conversation With Virginia Evans
item.description: Virginia Evans previously studied at James Madison University in Virginia before coming to Dublin to study at the Oscar Wilde Centre for Creative Writing. Now residing in North Carolina with her husband and children, Evans has pursued writing full time with her debut novel, The Correspondent, having been released in April 2025. item.title: Author Tim MacGabhann Launches Debut Poetry Collection
item.description: Novelist Tim MacGabhann launched his debut poetry collection, Found in a Context of Destruction, at Books Upstairs last Thursday, February 12th. Introduced by Jessica Traynor, novelist and poetry editor at Banshee Press, MacGabhann read a selection of poems from the collection for the first time. MacGabhann is the author of several novels, including The Black Pool, which explores themes of addiction and recovery. item.title: Kristen Stewart’s Take on Method Acting and What It Actually Means
item.description: In a December New York Times interview, Kristen Stewart commented on method acting, highlighting how the practice has become masculinised. “Have you ever heard of a female actor who was method?” seems to be her thesis statement. “Performance is inherently vulnerable and therefore quite embarrassing and unmasculine. item.title: The Female Tax On Emotion
item.description: “‘He’s not worth it’, that’s what they always say. But why do so many things seem to be worth more than women’s anger?” This quote from Annie Lord’s Notes on Heartbreak quite literally made me stop reading, put the book down and stare out the window for a good few minutes. item.title: Four Trinity Students Awarded With the John F Chambers Lennox Bursary
item.description: On the 18th of February four Trinity science students were awarded the Lennox bursary award, which is sponsored by Lennox Laboratory Supplies Ltd. To acknowledge their prowess in their academic success, Niamh Jordan (Neuroscience), Avaania Kapoor (Biological and Biomedical Sciences), Naomi Bennett (Geology), and Conor Mannion (Biochemistry) were each granted €1,904.60 to help them to continue their studies.
